title: Minimum Number of Coins to be Added
statement:
The array `coins` holds the values of the coins you own, and `target` is a positive integer. An amount `x` can be paid when some non-empty group of the coins, each coin used at most once, adds up to exactly `x`.

You may put extra coins into `coins`, choosing any positive value for each one. Return the smallest number of coins you have to put in so that every whole amount from `1` up to and including `target` can be paid.
notes:
## Intuition

Trying every set of extra coins and checking all subset sums is hopeless beyond tiny targets. Instead, track a single number `reach`: every amount from 1 to `reach` is already payable. A coin of value `c` with `c <= reach + 1` extends this to `reach + c`, because adding `c` to each amount in `[0, reach]` covers `[c, reach + c]` with no hole. If the smallest unused coin is bigger than `reach + 1`, nothing can ever pay `reach + 1`, so we must add a coin; the most useful one is exactly `reach + 1`, which stretches the range to `2 * reach + 1`.

## Approach

1. Sort `coins` so they are considered from smallest to largest. Start with `reach = 0`, `added = 0`, `index = 0`.
2. While `reach < target`:
   - if the next coin is at most `reach + 1`, use it: `reach += coins[index]` and move `index` on;
   - otherwise add a coin of value `reach + 1`: `reach` becomes `2 * reach + 1` and `added` grows by one.
3. Return `added`.

## Example 1, step by step

Sorted `coins = [1, 4, 10]`, `target = 19`.

- `reach = 0`: coin 1 fits, `reach = 1`.
- coin 4 > 2, so add 2: `reach = 3`, `added = 1`.
- coin 4 <= 4: `reach = 7`.
- coin 10 > 8, so add 8: `reach = 15`, `added = 2`.
- coin 10 <= 16: `reach = 25 >= 19`. The answer is `2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n + log target): sorting dominates; each added coin at least doubles `reach`.
- Space: O(1) beyond the sort.

## Pitfalls

- Sort numerically with `(a, b) => a - b`; the default sort compares digits as text.
- The test is `coins[index] <= reach + 1`, not `< reach + 1`: a coin equal to the first gap fills it.
- Stop as soon as `reach >= target`; leftover coins do not matter, and the loop must not run past the array.
- Adding any value smaller than `reach + 1` also works but grows the range less, so it can need more coins.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `reach` | every amount from 1 to `reach` can be paid |
| `added` | number of coins put in so far |
| `index` | position of the next unused coin in sorted `coins` |

narration.2: Sort the coins so the smallest unused one is always next.
narration.3: reach = 0 means no positive amount can be paid yet.
narration.7: Keep going until every amount up to target is payable.
narration.8: Can the next coin extend the covered range without leaving a hole at reach + 1?
narration.9: Yes: adding it to each payable amount covers everything up to reach + coin.
narration.10: That coin is used; move on to the next one.
narration.11: No coin can pay reach + 1, so one must be added.
narration.12: Adding a coin worth reach + 1 stretches the range to 2 * reach + 1, the farthest any single new coin can.
narration.13: Count the coin we put in.
narration.16: The whole range 1..target is covered; return how many coins were added.
